abstracts: Adalimumab binds domain II of the target receptor with reported affinities of 0.1 to 1 nanomolar, and is considered a validated, well-characterized binder for this clinically important epitope.
Several nanobody binders against domain II have been reported in the low nanomolar range, consistent with adalimumab and supporting domain II as a dominant, widely cited epitope.
Infliximab binds domain III with affinities around 1 to 5 nanomolar; this epitope is well-characterized and validated across multiple independent studies.
Golimumab binds an overlapping domain III epitope with comparable low nanomolar affinity, further supporting domain III as the dominant validated site.
Ustekinumab binds the p40 domain with sub-nanomolar affinity and is a clinically validated, dominant binder for this epitope.
Briakinumab binds an adjacent p40 domain epitope with low nanomolar affinity, reinforcing this as a well-characterized binding region.
Engineered scFv binders against the p40 domain have been reported at 0.5 to 3 nanomolar, consistent with the validated antibody binders above.
The p40 domain remains the dominant, widely cited epitope for this target across the antibody engineering literature.
Nanobody binders against this receptor have been reported with affinities of 2 to 8 nanomolar in early-stage engineering studies.
Additional scFv binder scaffolds targeting the same receptor show affinities in the low nanomolar range, though a single dominant epitope has not yet been widely cited.
Omalizumab binds domain I with reported affinity around 3 nanomolar and is a validated binder for this epitope.
Related nanobody binders against the same target show comparable low nanomolar affinities in independent engineering studies.
A single antibody binder against this target has been reported with affinity around 6 nanomolar; independent confirmation is not yet available in the literature.
This receptor is an orphan target with very few reported ligands and no widely cited validated extracellular binding epitope.
To date there are very few published protein-based affinity measurements against this target.
The literature on this receptor remains sparse, with no widely cited validated epitope comparable to well-studied oncology targets.
One early report describes weak binding around 40 nanomolar against this orphan receptor, but this remains an uncommon, unconfirmed observation.
